mcqs.learning_point: Taking the shape of a container
mcqs.question: Which statement best describes how a liquid takes the shape of its container?

options.A: A liquid keeps its own shape no matter what container it is placed in.
options.B: A liquid spreads out and adopts the shape of the bottom and sides of the container it occupies.
options.C: A liquid becomes a solid when it is poured into a narrow container.
options.D: A liquid evaporates instantly when it touches the walls of a container.

mcqs.answer: A liquid spreads out and adopts the shape of the bottom and sides of the container it occupies.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids have no fixed shape; they flow and fill the space available, conforming to the shape of the container. Option B correctly states this. Option A describes a solid, C is false, and D confuses evaporation with shape‑taking.

mcqs.question: Which of the following observations best shows the ability of a liquid to flow?

options.A: A glass of water remains motionless until the container is shaken.
options.B: Honey drips slowly from a spoon when it is lifted.
options.C: Ice cubes stay in the same place after being placed on a tray.
options.D: A balloon inflates when air is pumped into it.

mcqs.answer: Honey drips slowly from a spoon when it is lifted.
mcqs.explanation: Flow is the gradual movement of a liquid from one place to another. Honey dripping illustrates this property. Option A shows no flow, C is about a solid, and D describes a gas, not a liquid.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following is NOT an example of a liquid?
mcqs.explanation: Ice is the solid form of water, so it is not a liquid. Milk, motor oil, and mercury are all liquids at room temperature. Hence D is the correct answer.

mcqs.question: A 250 ml bottle of juice is poured into a wide glass. After pouring, the juice still occupies 250 ml in the glass. Which property of liquids does this illustrate?

options.A: Liquids take the shape of their container

mcqs.explanation: Even though the shape changes, the amount of liquid (its volume) remains the same, showing that liquids have a definite volume. Option A is true but does not explain the unchanged amount. Options C and D are incorrect for liquids under normal conditions.

mcqs.question: Which statement reflects a common misconception about liquids?

options.A: Liquids can change shape to fit any container.
options.B: Liquids have a fixed shape that cannot be altered.
options.C: Liquids flow from higher to lower places.
options.D: Liquids take the shape of the bottom of a container.

mcqs.answer: Liquids have a fixed shape that cannot be altered.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids do NOT have a fixed shape; they adapt to the shape of their container. Option B is the misconception. The other options correctly describe liquid behavior.

mcqs.learning_point: Taking the shape of a container
mcqs.question: Why does water poured into a tall, narrow bottle look different from water poured into a shallow, wide dish?

options.A: Water changes its chemical composition depending on the container shape.
options.B: Water always keeps the same shape, but our eyes are tricked by the container.
options.C: Water takes the shape of the container, so it fills the narrow bottle vertically and spreads out horizontally in the dish.
options.D: Water becomes a solid in narrow containers and remains liquid in wide ones.

mcqs.answer: Water takes the shape of the container, so it fills the narrow bottle vertically and spreads out horizontally in the dish.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids have no fixed shape; they conform to the shape of whatever holds them. Hence the observed difference is due to the container’s shape, not any change in the water itself. Options A, B, and D are scientifically incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which comparison correctly contrasts the ability to flow in liquids with that in solids?

options.A: Both liquids and solids flow equally well under gravity.
options.B: Liquids flow because their particles are loosely held, while solids retain shape because their particles are tightly packed.
options.C: Solids flow faster than liquids because they have less resistance.
options.D: Liquids cannot flow in narrow spaces, whereas solids can easily pass through small gaps.

mcqs.answer: Liquids flow because their particles are loosely held, while solids retain shape because their particles are tightly packed.
mcqs.explanation: In liquids, particles are close but not fixed, allowing them to slide past each other and flow. In solids, particles are in fixed positions, giving a definite shape and preventing flow. Options A, C, and D misrepresent the physical behavior of solids and liquids.

mcqs.question: A science competition asks: Identify the set that contains only liquids at room temperature (25 °C). Which set is correct?
mcqs.explanation: At 25 °C, mercury (metallic liquid), gasoline, and honey are all liquids. Option A includes air (gas) and sand (solid). Option C includes ice (solid) and steel (solid). Option D lists gases. Therefore B is the only set of liquids.
